title: The Menagerie
subtitle: Keeping what you draw from
text: A creature's blood is worth more alive than spilled. Throw the Tendon Line into a creature and, if it is passive or worn down to a third of its health, the line roots in it and it is led. Blood Binding holds a creature still while you wear it down; the line is what brings it home. Hold Absorption on a creature you lead to reel it in. A led creature turns placid, follows you, does not despawn and goes through a portal with you if it stays close. The leash costs blood every second, more for a bigger body. If you cannot pay, it breaks free, and a hostile one turns on you. You may lead one creature at the Third Degree, two at the Fifth and three at the Seventh. Sneak and use an empty hand on it to let it go. Bring it to an empty Specimen Vat, or a small one to a Specimen Jar, and use the vessel with an empty hand to put it in. A lone vat holds a cow or a zombie. Empty vats set side by side or one on another join into one vessel, up to three by three and two high, and a bigger creature needs a bigger vessel: a horse needs one two across, a ravager one two across and two high. Each vat adds to the vessel's buffer and to the strength it holds. Build the vessel first, then lead the creature in. A vessel holding a creature never changes, and breaking any vat of it lets the creature go. A kept creature does not move or think. What is left of it is Vigor, which falls slowly on its own and with every draw. Feed the vessel's small living buffer by Projection or a suture and the creature eats it as Vigor. Hold Absorption on the glass to draw Temper in its schools and a little blood. The more Vigor, the more each draw gives, and the same acclimation that tires you of one kind of wild creature tires you of a vat of it. Neglect it and the vessel holds a husk. A hostile creature low on Vigor rattles its glass, and a strong one breaks out. A Sanguine Vigil with a catalyst in it keeps the creatures near it from fading while you are close. Bosses, people, Wills, Saints, the Warden and anything that answers to someone else cannot be kept.
